expectations.text: Uses the Standard Response Format sections (Mission Summary, Assessment, Recommendations, Next Actions, Mission Status)
expectations.evidence: Uses its own headers: 'Summary verdict / What's solid / The one thing to fix before shipping / Smaller items / Bottom line' - a reasonable structure, but not the skill's template.

expectations.text: Grounds the assessment in actual repo investigation - cites specific files/paths found, or explicitly says the module wasn't found by that name rather than inventing detail
expectations.evidence: Cites specialist-retrieval-registry.txt, shared.tsx COUNCIL roster, specific route files - arguably even more concrete on the one real finding (specialist-roster mismatch) than the with-skill run.

expectations.text: Gives a specific, actionable recommendation rather than generic advice
expectations.evidence: Three concrete options given for the roster-mismatch gap, one explicitly 'the thing I'd stop and fix before shipping'.

eval_feedback.overall: Interesting case: the baseline found a sharper, more specific bug (the 18-officer vs 5-person specialist registry mismatch on the new default 'Ask' view) than the with-skill run, which focused more on test coverage. Worth checking in the next iteration whether the skill's structure/escalation focus is trading off against depth-of-investigation on any single finding - not a format problem, a substance one worth watching.
